phase: Landmark Phase B2, first church (geometry by day, estimated floodlighting at night)
object: Hedvigs kyrka, Norrköping (Nicodemus Tessin the Elder, consecrated 1673; renovated 2013–2014), with its bell tower

frame.description: Building frame: horizontal ground metres, origin = measured bell-tower centre, +u along the nave towards the east end (mean of the OSM long walls, way/88741182 vertices 59 → 43 and 7 → 19), +v towards the north; heights RH2000 metres.
frame.sceneContract: scene = (SWEREF 99 TM − (569030, 6494989)) / (25 · 0.9996584126), x east, z south; scene y = RH2000 / 25 (verticalOriginMetres 0)

OSM.accuracy: mapped from aerial imagery; typically ±1 m

LIDAR.what: Lantmäteriet point cloud, STAC collection dsm-skoglig-copc (called Laserdata NH 2020 elsewhere in this project)
LIDAR.accuracy: heights ±0.1–0.2 m on roofs; wall and tower-face positions ±0.3–0.5 m; thin tops under-sampled

PHOTO.what: Wikimedia Commons photographs, inspected as references only; nothing copied into the model

RAÄ.what: Arkeologerna / RAÄ UV Öst, Rapport 2015:7, 'Hedvigs kyrka – ett ledningsschakt för fasadbelysning runt kyrkan' (Rikard Hedvall)
facts: the parish (S:t Olofs församling) applied to install a new façade lighting on Hedvigs kyrka
cable trench just under 100 m along the church's east and west sides, north and south of the tower, and a short trench 5 m south-west of the tower
notStated: whether the lighting is in use in 2026

SEARCH.what: Search for evidence of current floodlighting
searched: Wikimedia Commons categories of the church (all 31 files daytime, 2005–2017)
norrkoping.se: Stad i ljus, Belysningsplan 2012-01-17, Riktlinje för belysning 2023

EST.what: estimate by this project, no measurement

values.evidence: highest non-noise return within 3 m of the tower centre (the needle; the vane above is not resolved)
nave section, median over u 6–24 of the highest return per 1 × 0.5 m cell: eave edge 15.0 at v −10.9/10.6, step at |v| ≈ 4.5 (20.7 → 22.1), ridge 25.4 at v ≈ 0

values.value: hipped with the same profile; ridge end u ≈ 26.5, step u ≈ 30.6

values.evidence: model adds ≈ 0.1–0.2 m (the percentiles lie inside the true edge); best-fitting rectangles turned 0–3°: the tower is aligned with the nave

values.value: lantern and its roof octagonal, chamfer 0.35 × smaller half-width
values.source: PHOTO (2012 close-up), LIDAR pattern (returns reach further at the side middles)

values.value: 2 arched louvres per face with gilded swags; clock dials Ø 1.6 m at 28.8 m on the wide lantern faces; gilded diamonds on the diagonal faces; gilded ball and needle
red brick, light stone plinth and cornice, cream frontispiece, copper roofs, dark panel-clad tower
round-arched 1.9 m wide, sill 7.8 m, top 13.2 m; 5 south, 3 north, 1 on each diagonal east wall
8 ground floodlights: west front 2 (6 500 cd, 24°/40°), tower 3 (24 000 / 2 × 20 000 cd, 9–10°/16–18°), east end 3 (7 000 cd, 18°/30°); 3000 K; on with the street lighting
values.source: RAÄ (that a lighting exists since 2014 and where its cables run) + EST (everything else)
values.evidence: computed ≈ 166 lx at mid-height of the west front, ≈ 61 lx on the bell stage's south face, ≈ 173 lx on the east wall (facadeIlluminance)
